A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Competency Gaps (CG) research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original concept-level analyses of Llama and Gemma, benchmark coverage, perturbation experiments, Chatbot Arena results and comparisons with other evaluation methods.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds three model evaluations, additional benchmark analyses, relevance annotations, a name-substitution experiment and an EvalTree reproduction.

M1.justification: The core activation averaging and CG scoring equations remain unchanged. Beyond v1's post-hoc concept selection, v2 introduces systematic benchmark-specific relevance labels and an optional variant that recomputes CG using the relevance-filtered dictionary (Appendix J).

E1.justification: V2 adds Qwen-based analyses of SWE-Bench, Terminal-Bench, MMLU, GPQA and Humanity's Last Exam (Appendix H), substantially extending task coverage. It also adds a controlled named-versus-unnamed reasoning scenario. The original ten-benchmark suite, Chatbot Arena and Real Toxicity comparison are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds an experimentally reproduced EvalTree comparison on MATH for all five models, with weakness-profile counts and qualitative comparisons against CG (Appendix P, Tables 39–41). This extends comparison to hierarchical capability discovery; the garak, AutoDetect and Arena-Hard-Auto comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1 and Qwen3-4B with their respective SAE/transcoder configurations. V2 also introduces support filters for new concept-example tables, named/unnamed prompt controls, systematic relevance annotation and an EvalTree evaluation configuration. The stated original Llama/Gemma setup is retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds a behavioral test of the Qwen foreign-name gap, systematic concept-relevance auditing, and checks connecting SWE-Bench repository coverage and MMLU historical omissions to identified gaps. These extend validation beyond the retained SAE-swapping, random-subsampling and adversarial-removal analyses.

E5.justification: V2 reports ten runs per condition for the new name-substitution test and confidence-based EvalTree weakness selection at alpha = 0.05. Existing 100-run subsampling, ten-repeat adversarial analyses and standard deviations are unchanged. The name experiment receives no confidence interval or significance test.

E6.justification: V2 adds model and benchmark score distributions, concept rankings, relevance percentages and EvalTree accuracies/profile counts. The new Qwen experiment reports 80% accuracy with unnamed protagonists versus 30% with Omar and Mahmoud. Earlier empirical plots and baseline results are retained, including all eleven Arena-Hard-Auto tables. Coverage skew is corrected from 'left' to 'right' without changing the plots.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 remain mathematically equivalent. V2 clarifies zero contributions from nonactivating benchmarks and adds an SAE primer, but these explain existing definitions rather than introduce substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain automated, representation-grounded discovery of model and benchmark gaps, concept-level decomposition complementing aggregate scores, and an exploratory tool. Broader demonstrations support these retained claims. Discovery of previously unstudied gaps was already claimed in v1 Section 4.2.2.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly separates concept activation from capability, acknowledges question-difficulty confounding, limits cross-SAE agreement to thematic correspondence and discusses filtering bias. It adds interpretations of the new model and behavioral results. Conversely, v1's discussion of missing label ground truth, SAE non-convergence and feature absorption is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds SAE/transcoder sources, dictionary-size and compute explanations, the relevance-annotation prompt and batch size, a stated relevance-label CSV release, and EvalTree configuration details. The code link remains unchanged. V1's explicit statement that extracted model/benchmark data accompany the code is omitted; this does not establish that those data were withdrawn.

R1.justification: V2 adds EvalTree positioning, describing its capability hierarchy as complementary to CG, and sources for new models, benchmarks and SAE background. It replaces the Vectara governance citation with a hallucination-leaderboard source and removes several SAE-limitations references. The broader related-work framing is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, workflow guidance and method exposition receive substantial editorial revision. V2 adds an explanatory SAE primer, separates design choices from limitations, reorganizes the appendices with a contents list, and moves the LLM-usage disclosure before the references.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text to two columns, redraws Figure 1, adds extensive model/benchmark plots and tables, and enlarges appendix screenshots. Existing case studies and the SAE-correspondence table move into appendices; v1's missing-concept Table 1 becomes prose. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens support for CG through broader model evaluations, relevance auditing, checked coverage omissions and the EvalTree comparison. Its explicit activation-versus-capability and difficulty-confounding caveats also improve interpretation. The net gain is limited by sparse protocols for the added benchmarks, the single-prompt name experiment with ten runs per condition, and removal of v1's fuller SAE-failure caveats.
